content.comment_body: Hello, I have a CECC-D PLC by [company_name], and I need it to work with a [product_name] by [company_name], with [company_name] as master and [product_name] as slave. I followed the same configuration as with the [company_name]-[company_name] [version_no], but it doesn't work. Is it possible? Thank you. [url]
The provided link is not accessible.

Hello, You can find the relevant archive here: [url] The document is titled [document]. On Codesys I followed all the steps, but I can't manage the configuration in the [product_name] software. Do I need any special setup in the [product_name] software, or is entering the IP address enough? I have set up the IP for [product_name], configured it as a slave, and connected its Ethernet port to the CECC-D, but Codesys doesn't detect the PLC. What can I do?
I'm sorry, I don't have any experience with Codesys.
Regarding [product_name], is it possible to make this work, or does it only function with [company_name] PLCs?

The example is for [company_name] PLC [version_no]. The [product_name] can't use the blocks from [version_no], and its communication protocol is different. The [product_name] version [version_no] or newer only supports Modbus TCP/IP. Does your modbus controller also use Modbus TCP/IP?
I have the [product_name] [version_no], and I need it to act as an extension for inputs and outputs using modbus communication, so that its digital signals are controllable by the CECC-D PLC.

I believe this is not feasible with the [product_name]. It can't communicate like the [version_no] series. The [product_name] is only able to read or write modbus addresses directly. Can you specify what the [product_name] needs to read (e.g. IR, HR, Coils)? What is the data format? I don't know.
[product_name] is connected to a 24VDC digital sensor, push buttons, and its outputs are wired to a solenoid valve; all signals are digital.
I'm sorry, I can't assist further in this situation. Our discussion may be getting off track.

analysis.insight_summary: The user attempted to link a [company_name] CECC-D PLC as a Modbus TCP master with a [product_name] [version_no] from [company_name] as a slave, aiming to use the [product_name] for remote digital I/O extension. Despite following documentation designed for [version_no], the communication was unsuccessful. Discussion clarified that [product_name] has different communication protocols and configuration needs compared to the [version_no] series, with its Modbus TCP/IP support presenting compatibility challenges in this use case.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the [product_name] [version_no] to operate as a Modbus slave that is compatible with a non-[company_name] master (the CECC-D), and hopes its digital inputs and outputs can be accessed and controlled as an extension module via Modbus TCP/IP.
